title.narrative: Provision of emergency life-saving WASH response packages to drought affected people and/or at risk of famine in Banadir (Daynile)

description.narrative: ltpgtAs per the Somalia Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2023, drought-induced displacement has increased fivefold since the beginning of 2022, with more than 1.3 million people displaced. Five regions, including Banadir, have received the biggest numbers of newly displaced people. About 95 percent live in urban areas where humanitarian conditions are dire and where spikes in displacement have strained the capacity of the humanitarian system to cope. The displaced have joined newly formed IDP sites or existing overcrowded settlements, further putting immense pressure on the limited basic services. Water shortages are at critical levels, exposing vulnerable people to additional risks. Furthermore, the risks of harassment and attacks increase in overcrowded and overused facilities, including in the waiting lines. In January 2023 alone, a total of 217 new cholera cases have been reported from 23 drought-affected districts, with most of the cases reported in three locations, including Banadir. Thus, in this project, SC aims to increase equitable and inclusive access to clean and safe drinking water and sanitation facilities and promote the adoption of safe hygiene practices for 17,037 people (4,259 women, 4,259 boys, 4090 men, and 4,429 girls), including 15% people with disabilities in Daynile district, where the risk of famine remains credible. This will help to reduce the risk of disease outbreaks while also meeting the immediate needs of the most vulnerable drought-affected and displaced communities to prevent loss of life and displacement caused by the drought. This will be accomplished by providing emergency water supply through vouchers for targeted communities and for nutrition and health services for a maximum of 60 days (7.5 liters per person) to ensure access to clean water for the most vulnerable people. The project will rehabilitate and equip of 2 strategic water sources targeting rural IDP communities to provide access to a reliable water supply for communities and health/nutrition facilities. To build community resilience and increase sustainability of WASH services, 14 village level WASH management committees will be capacitated to operate and maintain WASH facilities. 128 new emergency latrines with proper hand washing facilities and 19 disability friendly emergency sanitation facilities at IDP settlements will be constructed to improve safe excreta disposal and conduct community outreach hygiene promotion campaigns in AWD/Cholera to sensitize communities and nutrition/health facilities on preventive measures against water-related diseases through the village-based hygiene promoters. The project will also distribute 1500 hygiene kits sourced from regional hub located in Banadir region and 40 sets of sanitation tools to IDP communities to improve hygiene practices and mobilize the community for solid waste management. The project is designed to ensure equitable access to WASH services by older people and those with disabilities, the safety of children, and dignity and privacy for women and girls. The provision of immediate life-saving and sustainable solutions will contribute greatly to the reduction of morbidity/mortality and an improved sense of dignity, comfort, and security. Coordination with WASH clusters at national and state levels including PAH PMWDO NGOs implementing SHF SA1 2023 funded WASH projects in Deynile to avoid duplication in terms of site selections and water facilities planned for rehabilitation will be done in addition to ongoing coordination with key actors in Banadir in particular. Gender issues will be addressed through the collection of gender and age-disaggregated data, which will be analyzed to identify gaps, implement disability-inclusive and gender-sensitive interventions, and ensure people with disabilities and women's participation and empowerment. Protection of beneficiaries will be ensured during access and utilization of services in order to minimize future risks.lt/pgt
